new_statements.translation: 7.1. One form, different pronunciations. The acute accent ( ˊ ) is used on Malaweg words to mark the stress in pronouncing words and to distinguish the meanings of words that have the same spelling but different meanings. Examples: ána 'children' / aná 'child'; bátang 'part of a large tree' / batáng 'trap'; bílag 'strength' / bilág 'thing being dried'; pútut 'offspring' / putút 'trousers'. [sec. 1.2:] ... (1) the acute accent, which symbolizes stress or length ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is contrastive: it falls on either the penultimate or the final syllable and is not predictable from spelling, as shown by minimal pairs differing only in stress position (ána vs aná etc.); the orthography therefore marks it with an acute. No default position is stated. Reid's stress-marked Malaweg wordlist (1987) and syntax data (1993) are consistent with a penult/final lexical contrast (marked forms: 70 final, 31 penult, none earlier).
new_statements.exceptions: None; only the four minimal pairs are given. Sec. 1.2 equates the acute with 'stress or length' (diin o haba), implying stressed vowels are long, but this is not elaborated.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms in a community/pedagogical orthography (KWF/DepEd MTB-MLE series); not a linguist's phonological description. The only linguist-produced materials (Reid mss) mark stress on forms but give no rule.
new_statements.identity_note: All three saved sources describe the Malaweg/Malaueg of Rizal municipality, Cagayan (Glottolog mala1534; Ethnologue treats it as a dialect of Itawit [itv], Glottolog as a separate Ibanagic language). The KWF orthography spells the name Malawég (final stress).

sources.note: Ch. 7 'Pagbabalik sa tuldik' p.43 (Malaweg-language version p.42): the acute accent marks stress and distinguishes words spelled alike: ána 'children' vs aná 'child', bátang vs batáng, bílag vs bilág, pútut vs putút -- contrastive penult vs final stress. Sec. 1.2 (pp.16-17): the pahilis accent symbolizes 'diin o haba' (stress or length). No distributional rule given.
